title: I Paid the Parking Ticket I Earned and Not the One They Invented

parts.text: I photographed the missing sign before I even saw the ticket on the Civic. I am twenty-two, delivery driver, street smart about inches. The city had taken the no-parking sign down for a parade and forgotten it. The ticket still came, $65, cheerful. I had a timestamped photo of a naked pole and my hazard lights. The clerk, Dina, at the window had a candy dish of stale mints. I was polite like a person with evidence. They dismissed it in two weeks. Then I got a second ticket on a day I had actually parked dumb, in front of a hydrant by two feet, rushing a poke order. I paid that one the same day. People wanted me to fight both because I had won. Evidence is not a personality. The hydrant was real. The pole was naked. I still have the mint aftertaste in memory, dusty, sweet. Legal advice is sometimes just which photo you have. Dina said, "Do you have a photo of the pole" I said, "Yes, and I'll pay the hydrant one" Hasan said I should fight the hydrant too. I said I like sleeping. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened.

social.video_title: I fought the naked-pole ticket and paid the hydrant
social.description: Stale mints, a parade, two feet of dumb. Winning once is not a coupon. Would you have paid the second?
